rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose noun for a basin used to wash your hands or face.

example.english: The sink is in the bathroom; don’t put things in it.
example.traditional: 洗手盆喺廁所度，唔好擺雜物喺入面。
example.jyutping: sai2 sau2 pun4 hai2 ci3 so2 dou6 m4 hou2 baai2 zaap6 mat6 hai2 jap6 min6

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for a person or object going below the surface, especially in water.

example.english: The boat is about to sink.
example.jyutping: zek3 syun4 zau6 faai3 cam4 laa3

rows.note: Use this for the drain or outlet that carries wastewater away.

example.english: The sink’s drain is blocked, so the water won’t run off.
example.traditional: 去水位塞咗，啲水流唔走。
example.jyutping: heoi3 seoi2 wai2 sak1 zo2 di1 seoi2 lau4 m4 zau2

rows.note: Use this idiomatic phrase for a sudden feeling of dread, disappointment, or apprehension.

example.english: When I heard the bad news, I felt my heart sink.
example.traditional: 一聽到個壞消息，我個心一沉。
example.jyutping: jat1 teng1 dou2 go3 waai6 siu1 sik1 ngo5 go3 sam1 jat1 cam4

rows.note: Use this when something is driven or pushed into another thing, such as a nail into wood.

example.english: They used a hammer to sink the nail into the board.
example.traditional: 佢用鎚仔將支釘打入木板。
example.jyutping: keoi5 jung6 ceoi4 zai2 zoeng1 zi1 deng1 daa2 jap6 muk6 baan2

rows.note: Use this colloquial verb when an action causes a boat or ship to go under.

example.english: The storm caused the cargo ship to sink.
example.jyutping: coeng4 fung1 bou6 zing2 cam4 zo2 sau1 fo3 syun4
